1:56 to 75mm Miniature Scale for 3D Printing

The exact slicer percentage to go from 1:56 to 75mm. I calculated this from a 175cm human baseline and printed it myself before posting.

The math

(75.0mm / 31.3mm) × 100 = 240.0%

Based on 175cm human baseline, eye-level measurement (160cm).

Scale baselines

  • Source eye level28.6mm Eye
  • Target eye level75.0mm Eye
  • Scale factor240.0%

How I got this number

By kitsorix, 3D printing hobbyist

This percentage comes from a 175cm human baseline with eye-level at 160cm. I print the result on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini and measure with digital calipers before I post it. If it looks wrong on my table, I adjust it.

I test every percentage on FDM before publishing. PLA and PETG cool with minimal dimensional change — typically under 0.5%. If a number fails on my machine, I adjust it.

Full methodology →

When you need this

You will need this when bringing older or smaller 1:56 models into a modern 75mm collection. This is a big upscale. Models will look like different species next to each other unless you apply the conversion to the whole unit or army.

Source: 1:56

1:56 is the ratio. Often paired with 28mm infantry. Tanks and vehicles at 1:56 look correct next to 28mm miniatures. You will see it in: Bolt Action, Chain of Command, Gaslands.

Note: Some manufacturers label 1:48 vehicles as 'compatible with 28mm.' They are slightly oversized.

Target: 75mm

75mm shows up in: Display busts, Miniature painting competitions, Scale 75 display line. Not a tabletop wargaming scale. Designed for contest judging and display cabinets.

Note: 75mm sculpts often have separate heads or arms for easier painting access.

Print notes

Set your slicer to 240.0%. 75mm on FDM needs a 0.2mm nozzle and very slow print speeds for acceptable surface quality.
